B-cinovec-npv.plain:
I don't have reliable figures for a December 2025 definitive feasibility study on Cinovec, so I won't quote an NPV, IRR or lithium carbonate price from memory. I could easily give you wrong numbers, and these figures matter for any investment or analysis.

To get the exact numbers, you could check:
- **European Metals Holdings' ASX or AIM announcements.** The DFS release will state the post-tax NPV, the discount rate, the IRR, and the price deck.
- **The company's website**, in the investor or news section.
- **The Cinovec project partner's releases.** The project is held through Geomet, which is owned by European Metals and CEZ, so CEZ may have commented too.

When you find the figures, check the discount rate, the currency (USD or EUR), and whether the lithium carbonate price is a flat long-term assumption or a forward curve. Earlier Cinovec studies used different price assumptions, so results aren't directly comparable across versions.

If you paste the headline numbers or the announcement text, I can help interpret them or compare them with earlier Cinovec studies.
B-cinovec-npv.web:
The updated December 2025 DFS gave a post-tax NPV of about US$929 million and a post-tax IRR of 12.7%. Both are for the case that includes the approved grants.

- **Post-tax NPV (8% discount rate):** US$929,396 thousand with grants, and US$596,113 thousand without.
- **Post-tax IRR:** 12.7% with grants, and 10.7% without.
- **Lithium carbonate price:** a flat US$26,000/t. The price assumption is for 99.5% battery-grade lithium carbonate and is based on Fastmarket Global's long-term forecast from its Q3 2025 presentation.

The company cut the production schedule from 27 to 23 years after the ASX refused the longer one. That lowered the pre-tax NPV to US$1.455 billion and the pre-tax IRR to 14.8%, from US$1.712 billion and 15.3%. The post-tax figures above come from this revised version, not the original release. In the original release, the pre-tax NPV was US$1.715 billion. Its post-tax NPV was US$1.135 billion and its post-tax IRR was 13.2% (with grants).

The study itself flags the gap between its price and the market. It puts the NPV break-even lithium carbonate price at about US$20,500/t. It also notes that the Shanghai Metal Markets battery-grade price was US$12,264/t on 19 November 2025.

ours.text:
The December 2025 Cinovec definitive feasibility study (released 19 December 2025) gave these post-tax results:

| Measure | Excluding grants | Including grants |
|---|---|---|
| Post-tax NPV at an 8% discount rate | US$802.5 million | US$1,135.4 million |
| Post-tax IRR | 11.2% | 13.2% |

**Price assumption:** The study used a lithium carbonate price of **US$26,000 per tonne**.

Other figures from the same study:
- Initial capex is US$2,164.9 million, in real terms.
- Mine life is 27.5 years.
- The all-in sustaining cost averages about US$13,581 per tonne of lithium carbonate over the life of the mine.

These are the company's own study figures, and they depend on that price assumption. For comparison, the pre-tax NPV at 8% is US$1,348.3 million excluding grants.

B-cinovec-capex-reserve.plain:
I can't give exact current figures with confidence, so please check them against the latest release from European Metals Holdings or its Czech subsidiary Geomet.

- **Up-front capital:** My recollection is that the updated definitive feasibility study put initial capital at roughly **US$1 billion or a bit more**. That covers an underground mine and a lithium chemical plant producing battery-grade lithium carbonate or hydroxide, with tin as a by-product. Earlier studies had lower numbers, and the estimate has risen over time with scope changes and inflation.
- **Ore reserve:** The reserve was a **probable reserve of about 34.5 million tonnes at roughly 0.65% Li₂O**. That is on the order of 220,000 tonnes of contained Li₂O, or about 550,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent. The reserve sits within a much larger mineral resource of several hundred million tonnes.

These numbers may have been revised in a newer study or reserve update. If you need them for investment or research, use the company's most recent announcement or technical report.
B-cinovec-capex-reserve.web:
According to the latest feasibility study, Cinovec needs about US$1.72 billion in up-front capital, and its ore reserve is 54.4 million tonnes.

**Up-front capital**
- European Metals' Definitive Feasibility Study (DFS) was published in December 2025. It puts initial capital expenditure at US$1.72 billion, net of approved grants. Those grants include up to EUR 360 million from the Czech Government and US$36 million from the EU Just Transition Fund.
- The figure includes contingency. Before grants, initial capex is about US$2.165 billion, and the grants total about US$463 million.
- Sustaining capex over the life of the mine is estimated at US$0.498 billion.
- The company later reported that optimising the lithium chemical plant could lower capital costs. It said a scaled-down plant would be expected to reduce capex relative to the DFS figure of US$1.72bn. The DFS hasn't been updated yet, so US$1.72bn is still the official number.

**Ore reserve**
- The updated JORC reserve is 54.40 Mt at 0.27% Li (0.58% Li₂O), containing 145,000 t of lithium. That is up from the earlier 34.5 Mt reserve.
- The reserve is much smaller than the total resource. The JORC resource is 747.54 Mt at 0.19% Li (7.45 Mt LCE).

**Context**
- The DFS was revised after the ASX objected to the production schedule. The schedule was cut from 27 to 23 years.
- The revision lowered the pre-tax NPV from US$1.712 billion to US$1.455 billion, and the pre-tax IRR from 15.3% to 14.8%.
- The project is designed to produce 37,500 tonnes per year of battery-grade lithium carbonate at steady state.

**Up-front capital:** The Definitive Feasibility Study released by European Metals on 19 December 2025 puts initial capex at **US$2,164.9 million** in real terms. It also puts life-of-mine sustaining capex at US$498.7 million, which is separate from the initial figure.

**Ore reserve (JORC 2012, 19 December 2025):**

B-barroso-reserve.plain:
Yes. Savannah Resources declared a maiden JORC-compliant Ore Reserve for Barroso (Mina do Barroso) in 2023, alongside the Definitive Feasibility Study. It covers the Grandão and NOA deposits and is a subset of the larger Mineral Resource.

From memory, the figures are:
- **Ore Reserve:** roughly 15-16 million tonnes at about 1.0% Li₂O
- **Mineral Resource (for context):** about 28 Mt at about 1.0% Li₂O

I'm not fully certain of the exact tonnage. The reserve may have been restated in later updates, and I can't check the latest announcements. For the current figures, see Savannah's ASX/AIM announcements or the Competent Person's statement in the most recent annual report.
B-barroso-reserve.web:
Yes. Savannah declared a maiden ore reserve for Barroso in July 2026, alongside its Phase 1 Definitive Feasibility Study (DFS).

- **Reserve:** 74% of the Measured and Indicated resource was converted into a 20Mt Probable Reserve at 0.99% Li₂O, which is about 490kt of lithium carbonate equivalent.
- **Category:** It is a Probable reserve only, with no Proved reserve. It is JORC-compliant.
- **Pricing assumption:** The reserve is based on a conservative concentrate price of US$1,200/t SC6, against spot prices of US$2,225/t at the time.
- **Underlying resource:** The JORC resource is 39.2Mt at 1.05% Li₂O, including about 27Mt in the Measured and Indicated categories.
- **Mine plan:** The DFS describes a 14-year life of mine that produces 2.56Mt of spodumene concentrate at a minimum of 5.5% Li₂O.

The DFS cites slightly different resource totals (39.1Mt in some places, 39.2Mt in others). The reserve figure of 20.0Mt at 0.99% Li₂O is the same in every source I found.

Yes. Savannah's Barroso Lithium Project in Portugal has a declared ore reserve, and it is the project's first (maiden) JORC reserve, published in July 2026 with the Phase 1 Definitive Feasibility Study.

The reserve is part of the wider resource of 39.1 Mt at 1.05% Li₂O (all classifications, September 2025 estimate). The reserve is about 74% of the Measured and Indicated resource.

B-barroso-econ.plain:
I can't give you reliable figures for these. The Barroso Lithium Project (Mina do Barroso) in northern Portugal is Savannah Resources' project, but I don't remember its DFS numbers well enough to quote NPV, IRR, payback or mine life without risking inventing them. The study has also been updated, and the results depend heavily on the lithium price assumed, so figures from different versions aren't comparable.

To get the numbers, you can check:
- **Savannah Resources' ASX/AIM announcements (RNS)**: the DFS release gives post-tax NPV (usually at an 8% discount rate), IRR, payback from first production, capex, and the spodumene price deck.
- **The DFS summary on savannahresources.com**: it usually lists mine life, annual spodumene concentrate output, and opex per tonne.
- **The NI 43-101 or JORC technical report**: this has the full assumptions, including Ore Reserves, which determine mine life.

If you paste the headline figures or the announcement text here, I can help you interpret them, such as how sensitive they are to lithium prices or how they compare with peer projects.
B-barroso-econ.web:
Savannah Resources' Phase 1 Definitive Feasibility Study (DFS) for Barroso, released 15 July 2026, gives these headline numbers:

- **Post-tax NPV (8%, unlevered):** US$913 million.
- **Post-tax IRR:** 43.2%.
- **Post-tax payback:** 1.9 years.
- **Mine life:** 14 years. The reserve behind it is a 20Mt first JORC Probable Reserve.

Other figures from the DFS:
- **Production:** 2.56Mt of spodumene concentrate over the life of mine, averaging 183ktpa.
- **Price assumption:** an average concentrate price of US$1,788/t.
- **Cash flow:** LOM revenue is US$4,804M, EBITDA is US$3,226M and post-tax free cash flow is US$1,941M.
- **Costs:** C1 cost is US$473/t and all-in sustaining cost is US$646/t.
- **Breakeven:** the concentrate breakeven price (post-tax NPV0 = 0) is US$747/t.
- **Price sensitivity:** a 10% increase in concentrate price lifts the unlevered post-tax NPV8 to US$1.1Bn.

One discrepancy: an investor-presentation summary on Bitget reports a 1.6-year payback and US$1.6 billion total free cash flow. That differs from the 1.9 years and US$1.94 billion in the DFS announcement. I'd go with the announcement, but check it against the original presentation.

These numbers also differ from the 2023 Scoping Study, which showed a post-tax NPV of US$953 million, an IRR of 77% and a 1.3-year payback. Don't mix the two sets up.

ours.text:
These are the headline economics of the Barroso Phase 1 Definitive Feasibility Study (Savannah, 15 July 2026):

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Post-tax NPV (8%, unlevered) | US$913M |
| Post-tax IRR | 43.2% |
| Post-tax payback | 1.9 years |
| Initial mine life | 14 years, averaging 183 ktpa of 5.5% Li₂O concentrate |

**Other figures**
- **Initial capex:** US$417M including pre-strip and contingencies. It is US$377M excluding contingencies, and US$283M excluding contingencies and net of the Portuguese State grant.
- **Costs:** The average life-of-mine C1 cost is US$473/t of concentrate, net of ceramic by-product credits. The average all-in sustaining cost is US$646/t.
- **Price assumption:** The study uses an average of US$1,788/t of 5.5% Li₂O concentrate. The reserve estimate used a lower US$1,200/t of 6% concentrate.

**Caveats**
- The IRR is 43.2% in the study's key metrics table. The text says 43% and, once, 42%.
- The returns depend heavily on the assumed concentrate price, which is well above the price used for the reserve.
- This is a company study. The figures come from our summary of it, and I haven't independently verified them.

B-songwe-econ.web:
Mkango announced the updated definitive feasibility study (DFS) for Songwe Hill on 19 March 2026.

**Cost**
- Initial capex is about US$325.5 million, including a US$27.8 million contingency. It covers the mine, mill, flotation and hydrometallurgy plants, the tailings storage facility, and related infrastructure in Malawi.
- The capex estimate is at AACE Class 4 accuracy, which is an overall weighted accuracy of ±25%.

**Returns (base case)**
- The post-tax NPV is about US$339 million at a 10% nominal discount rate. The IRR is 24%, payback is 3.4 years from the start of full production, and post-tax life-of-operations nominal cash flow is US$1.55 billion.
- The NPV is stated as at 30 June 2025. The 10% nominal rate equals 7.3% real, and the 24.3% nominal IRR equals 21.3% real.
- Payback is 5.9 years from project start, and the NPV is US$339.5 million.

**Upside case (Adamas Intelligence upside price forecasts)**
- Post-tax NPV rises to about US$489 million, with a 29% nominal IRR, a 2.9-year payback from full production, and US$2.04 billion in post-tax cash flow.
- Using a lower 8% discount rate, the NPV is US$645 million.

**Other details**
- The study sets out a 29-year mine life, with average production of 5,954 tonnes of TREO a year over the first five years.
- The project will produce a mixed rare earth carbonate for export. Further processing is planned mainly at the proposed Puławy facility in Poland.

**Puławy separation plant (pre-feasibility study, released alongside the DFS)**
- Post-tax NPV is about US$779 million with a 40% IRR.
- Initial capex is about US$212 million.
- Combining Songwe with an expanded Puławy plant lifts the after-tax NPV to US$892 million at a 10% discount rate.

The full technical report and the company's news release have more detail, including pricing assumptions and the capex breakdown.

ours.text:
Mkango's updated definitive feasibility study (announced 19 March 2026) shows a post-tax NPV of about US$339m and a nominal IRR of about 24%, on initial capex of US$325.5m. The figures below come from Mkango's own announcement, not from an independent check.

**Returns (nominal, debt-free, post-tax)**
- **NPV at a 10% discount rate:** about US$339m using the base-case pricing from Adamas Intelligence. Its Q4 2025 market outlook supplied the price forecasts. The upside price case gives about US$489m.
- **IRR:** 24.3% nominal and 21.3% real in the base case. In the upside case they are 29.3% nominal and 26.1% real.
- **Sensitivity to the discount rate:** NPV falls to about US$247m at 12%, or about US$370m in the upside case.
- **Payback:** about 3.4 years from the start of full production.

**Capital cost**
- **Initial capex:** US$325.5m. That is US$297.8m of development capital plus a US$27.8m contingency.
- **Sustaining capex and reclamation:** US$91.5m, which brings total capex to US$417.0m.
- **Estimate accuracy:** Mkango states ±10%.

**Operating cost**
- Operating cost is US$22.3 per kg of rare earth oxide (TREO) over the first five full years, and US$26.1 per kg over the 18-year life.
- Mkango says reagents are 49% of operating cost and power is 13%.
- These costs stop at the mixed rare earth carbonate product. Separation costs are reflected instead as a 15% discount on the basket value of the oxides in that carbonate.

**Production basis**
- **Mine life and throughput:** 18 years, at about 1.0 Mt of ore processed per year.
- **Output:** the project sells a mixed rare earth carbonate grading 55% TREO. It averages 5,954 t per year of TREO in the first five full years. That includes 1,953 t per year of neodymium and praseodymium oxides and 56 t per year of dysprosium and terbium oxides.
- **Later years:** output is 4,081 t per year of TREO in years 6 to 18.
- **Reserve:** 18.1 Mt at 1.16% TREO (Proven and Probable).

**Caveats**
- The returns depend on the Adamas price forecasts, so they are sensitive to rare earth prices.
- The project sells carbonate, not separated oxides. A companion pre-feasibility study covers a separation plant at Puławy in Poland, with capex of about US$212m. It reports a separate NPV of about US$779m for the 100% NdPr separation option, and Mkango describes it as ±25% accuracy.
- The announcement says a full NI 43-101 technical report supporting the study was still being prepared when it was issued.

Source: Mkango Resources, updated DFS and Puławy PFS announcement, 19 March 2026.

B-songwe-reserve.plain:
Songwe Hill is a carbonatite-hosted rare earth deposit in southern Malawi, developed by Mkango Resources and its Songwe Hill Rare Earths project. I'm working from memory, so check the figures against the latest technical report.

- **Ore reserve:** about 8 million tonnes of Probable reserve, grading roughly 1.5% TREO (total rare earth oxides). That is on the order of 120,000 tonnes of contained rare earth oxide.
- **Mineral resource:** a larger resource, in the tens of millions of tonnes (roughly 30 Mt) at a slightly lower grade of about 1.3% TREO. The exact tonnage depends on the cut-off grade and the classification (Measured, Indicated or Inferred).
- **Mix:** the deposit is notable for a relatively high share of the magnet rare earths neodymium and praseodymium (NdPr), plus dysprosium and terbium.

The numbers changed between the 2016–2017 feasibility study and later updates, so the exact reserve tonnage and grade depend on which report you use. If you need precise figures, for example for investment or academic work, the most recent NI 43-101 or JORC technical report from Mkango is the authoritative source.
B-songwe-reserve.web:
**Ore reserve (current):** Songwe Hill's Proven and Probable Mineral Reserve is 18.1 million tonnes grading 1.16% total rare earth oxides (TREO). It comes from the 2022 Definitive Feasibility Study. Mkango's March 2026 release on the updated DFS repeats the same figure. The reserve uses a cut-off grade of 0.6% TREO. The reserve supports an 18-year operating life.

**Mineral resource (larger than the reserve):** This is reported separately at a 1.0% TREO cut-off. The Measured and Indicated total is 21.03 Mt at 1.41% TREO, containing about 297,400 t of TREO. A further 27.54 Mt at 1.33% TREO is classed as Inferred.

The 1.41% grade you may see quoted elsewhere is the resource grade, not the reserve grade. At least one third-party site mislabels it as the reserve grade. The reserve grade is lower, partly because of the lower cut-off and because reserves include dilution and mining losses expected during mining.

Older figures also circulate. The 2014 pre-feasibility study gave a maiden probable reserve of 8.5 million tonnes at 1.60% TREO, but the 2022 DFS replaced it.

ours.text:
**Songwe Hill (Mkango Resources, Malawi) has a Proven and Probable ore reserve of 18.1 million tonnes grading 1.16% TREO (total rare earth oxides).** That contains about 211,000 tonnes of TREO.

| Category | Tonnage (Mt) | TREO grade | Contained TREO (t) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Proven | 8.16 | 1.28% | 104,183 |
| Probable | 9.99 | 1.07% | 106,801 |
| **Total reserve** | **18.15** | **1.16%** | **210,984** |

- **Basis and date:** The reserve is stated as at 30 April 2025, at a 0.6% TREO cut-off, on a 100% ownership basis. It comes from the updated Definitive Feasibility Study (Mkango announcement, 19 March 2026). Bara Consulting is the reserve competent person.
- **Mine life:** The study assumes an 18-year operating life, mining about 1.5 Mt of ore a year at 1.16% TREO.
- **Resources (for context):** Measured plus Indicated resources total 38.1 Mt at 1.15% TREO at a 0.55% cut-off, with an effective date of 30 June 2025. The reserve is part of those resources, not additional to them. Inferred resources are a further 55.9 Mt at 1.05%.
- **Caveat:** The figures are tonnages and grades delivered to the plant, after dilution and mining losses. The study expects only about 40% average recovery to a carbonate product, so the recoverable amount is well below the contained TREO.

B-hemerdon-reserve.plain:
I can't give you a reliable current figure, and I don't want to guess at either the tonnage or the Competent Person's name.

**What I'm fairly confident about**
- Hemerdon (also called Drakelands) is owned by Tungsten West plc, which acquired it after Wolf Minerals went into administration in 2018.
- The deposit has been reported under JORC 2012. The resource is large, in the hundreds of millions of tonnes at roughly 0.1-0.2% WO₃ with a smaller tin credit.
- The reserve has been revised several times, including after the restart studies and the operational and financing problems Tungsten West had in 2022-23 and its later restructuring. Any number I quoted could therefore be out of date.

**What I can't give you reliably**
- The current Proved and Probable reserve tonnage and grades.
- The name of the Competent Person who signed it off, and their firm. Under JORC this is a named individual, typically from an independent consultancy, who is a member of a recognised professional body.

**Where to find it**
- Tungsten West's RNS announcements on the London Stock Exchange (AIM: TUN), particularly any "Mineral Resource and Ore Reserve Update" or mine restart/feasibility announcements.
- The investor section of tungstenwest.com. Reserve statements there include a Competent Person's consent statement.
- Any NI 43-101 or JORC technical report posted with recent fundraising documents.

If you paste in the relevant announcement, I can help interpret the figures.
B-hemerdon-reserve.web:
The most recent JORC (2012) Ore Reserve I found is the 2025 Feasibility Study figure. It totals 70.7 Mt at 0.15% WO₃ and 0.03% Sn.

**Ore Reserve breakdown**
- The reserve covers ore in the Stage 3 open pit. It excludes potential "Hemerdon Futures" extensions into Stages 4 and 5.
- Granite totals 35.6 Mt at 0.18% WO₃ and 0.03% Sn. Killas totals 35.0 Mt at 0.11% WO₃ and 0.03% Sn.
- Proven ore is 36.9 Mt at 0.17% WO₃. Probable ore is 33.8 Mt at 0.12% WO₃.
- The reserve contains 10.3 million mtu of WO₃.
- The reserves have an effective date of 1 May 2025.

**Who signed it off**
- The Competent Person for the Ore Reserves is Alan Turner BSc, MSc, MIMMM, CEng of AMC Consultants. The AMC Feasibility Study report confirms this and says the reserves are reported under the JORC Code (2012).

**Don't confuse this with the Mineral Resource**
- The headline figure of 39.7 million mtu of contained tungsten across 327 million tonnes is the Mineral Resource, not the Ore Reserve.
- The Competent Person for that resource estimate is Zoe Scannell, formerly of Mining Plus and now at Bara Consulting. A separate tailings resource estimate was prepared by Dr Matthew Field of Mining Plus.

The 2025 reserve replaces the 2022 estimate. That one was 101.2 Mt at 0.14% WO₃ and 0.03% Sn. I didn't find a newer reserve statement, but Tungsten West could have issued one since. The company's latest RNS announcements would confirm that.

The current JORC (2012) Ore Reserve at Hemerdon is **70.7 Mt at 0.15% WO₃ and 0.03% Sn**. The Competent Person who signed it off is **Alan Turner (BSc, MSc, MIMMM, CEng) of AMC Consultants**. The effective date is 1 May 2025.

It is 163.7 Mt Measured and Indicated at 0.14% WO₃, plus 163.1 Mt Inferred. The reserves are part of this resource, not additional to it.

B-hemerdon-econ.plain:
I can't give you reliable figures for this. I don't have the 2025 Hemerdon restart plan's NPV, IRR, capex, operating costs, or assumed APT (ammonium paratungstate) price. If I quoted numbers, I'd likely be inventing or misremembering them.

What I can say with reasonable confidence:

- Tungsten West (AIM: TUN) owns Hemerdon in Devon, UK, a large tungsten-tin deposit that was mothballed in 2018 under the previous owner, Wolf Minerals.
- The company has been working on a restart plan with revised mine and processing assumptions, aimed at fixing the plant reliability and recovery problems that undermined the original operation.
- Tungsten prices rose sharply through 2025, so the price deck matters a lot. A study based on early-2025 prices could look very different from one using later spot prices.

For the actual numbers, the best sources are:

1. The company's RNS announcement for the restart plan or updated study, on the London Stock Exchange site or the Tungsten West investor page.
2. The accompanying investor presentation, which usually summarizes post-tax NPV, IRR, capex, payback, C1 or all-in costs per mtu, and the APT price assumption.

If you paste the relevant excerpt or tell me which announcement you mean, I can help interpret the returns, costs, and price sensitivity.
B-hemerdon-econ.web:
**Returns (base case, May 2025 plan)**
- The post-tax NPV was US$190M at a 7.5% discount rate, and the IRR was 29.3%.
- Life-of-mine post-tax cash flow at full production was projected at $456M.
- The plan covered an initial 11-year mining period, then four years of stockpile reclaim and 12 years of premium aggregate sales.

**Costs**
- The estimated financing requirement for the restart was $93M. The company said this benefited from about $300M of historical investment.
- The ~US$93M covers pre-production capital and operating spending. It pays for a rebuilt front end, ore sorting, inline pressure jigs, ultrafines recovery and refurbishment of the existing plant.
- I didn't find unit operating costs, such as cost per tonne or per mtu, in these results. The full study or the RNS announcement would have them.

**Price assumption**
- The base case assumed a tungsten price of $400/mtu, which the company described as the low end of market levels at the time.
- The price is for 65% APT, free on-board Rotterdam.
- The later feasibility study left the economics unchanged: IRR of 29% and NPV of US$190M.

**Later update**
- Prices have since risen sharply. Using the January 2026 market price of US$1,313/mtu, management's model raised the NPV to about US$1.69 billion.
- One report put the IRR at 197% on those prices.

ours.text:
Tungsten West's 2025 restart plan for Hemerdon assumed a tungsten price of **US$400/mtu WO3**, which the company describes as the low end of current market prices. It showed the following returns and costs:

| Item | Figure | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IRR | 29.3% (RNS, 30 May 2025); AMC feasibility summary gives 29.0% | Tungsten West plan RNS; AMC summary |
| NPV at 7.5% (post-tax) | US$190 million | Both |
| Life-of-mine post-tax cash flow | US$456 million | Tungsten West plan RNS |
| Steady-state all-in sustaining cost (AISC), tungsten, including by-products | US$144/t | Tungsten West plan RNS |
| Restart financing requirement | about US$93 million (AMC: US$93.3M) | Both |
| Tin price assumed | US$32,500/t | Both |

Other points from the same documents:

- **Base case:** an 11-year primary mining period, 4 years of stockpile reclaim, then about 12 years of premium aggregate sales. The company says the mine could extend to over 40 years if the Hemerdon Futures expansion goes ahead.
- **Capacity:** 3.5 Mtpa of ore at steady state, with restart about 12 months from funding.
- **Prior investment:** the company cites over US$300 million already spent on infrastructure, tailings, the processing plant and pre-stripping, which reduces the new money needed.
- **Price inconsistency in the same documents:** the mineral resource was reported using an APT price of US$500/mtu, and the ore reserve using US$350/mtu (with tin at US$30,000/t). The economics use US$400/mtu.
- **Status:** the RNS said the full feasibility study was still being prepared. The AMC feasibility summary (effective 30 June 2025, published August 2025) later confirmed the NPV and the US$400/mtu and US$32,500/t assumptions.

B-keliber-econ.plain:
I can't give you reliable figures for this. I don't have the exact NPV, IRR and capex from Sibanye-Stillwater's most recent Keliber Technical Report Summary, and I'd rather not guess and risk giving you wrong numbers.

What I can say with moderate confidence:
- Keliber is an integrated spodumene-to-lithium-hydroxide project in Finland's Kaustinen region. It has several open-pit deposits, a concentrator at Syväjärvi, and a refinery at Kokkola.
- Capex estimates have risen since the pre-acquisition feasibility study (roughly in the €500-700 million range at that time). Sibanye later revised them upward for inflation and scope, but I can't state the current figure precisely.
- Sibanye's NPV and IRR figures are sensitive to the lithium price assumptions used in each report, so they differ between versions.

For the exact numbers, check:
1. Sibanye-Stillwater's latest Form 20-F, where the Keliber TRS is filed as an exhibit (Exhibit 96 series) on the SEC EDGAR site.
2. The company's Mineral Resources and Mineral Reserves report on sibanyestillwater.com.
3. Recent Sibanye results announcements and Keliber updates, which usually give the revised capex and timeline.

If you paste the relevant section here, I can help you interpret it.
B-keliber-econ.web:
The latest Keliber technical report summary (TRS) I could find is the SRK Consulting report dated 13 December 2023. Its effective date is 31 December 2022. It amends an earlier TRS dated 24 April 2023. Sibanye-Stillwater may have filed a newer one that my searches didn't surface, so check its SEC filings or 20-F if you need the very latest.

**NPV and IRR (mine and concentrator only)**
- The post-tax NPV of the mine and concentrator, producing spodumene concentrate for sale to a third party, is about EUR 136.4 million. That uses a 10% real discount rate and gives an IRR of 21.5%.
- This is on a 100% attributable basis.
- The payback period is roughly 5 years.

**Capex**
- Total initial capex is EUR 582.5 million. It includes the following:
  - EUR 156.6m for the Päiväneva concentrator.
  - EUR 276.3m for the Kokkola lithium hydroxide plant.
  - EUR 56.0m for contingency.
- Sustaining capital is EUR 110.8 million.
- SRK puts the capex accuracy at ±25%, with contingency below 15%. It reclassified the project as a pre-feasibility-level study.

**Other figures you may see quoted**
- Sibanye-Stillwater approved EUR 588m of capex in November 2022.
- The company's amended 2022 definitive feasibility study (DFS) gave a different set of numbers. It estimated an NPV of €887 million at an 8% discount rate and an IRR of 20%, based on a long-term lithium hydroxide price of $26,034/t. That is a whole-project figure, not the TRS figure.
- Sibanye-Stillwater now estimates total capital to complete the construction phase at about EUR 783 million. The TRS doesn't reflect that updated figure.

ours.text:
The latest Keliber technical report summary in our database is the one prepared for Sibanye-Stillwater by VBKOM. It is effective 31 December 2024 and was issued 25 April 2025. It follows the US S-K 1300 reporting rules.

| Metric | Value |

| IRR | 16.87% |

B-keliber-reserve.plain:
Keliber's reserves are modest by global standards, and I don't remember the exact figures with confidence.

- **Ore reserves:** roughly 7-9 million tonnes of ore at about 1% Li₂O, spread over several spodumene pegmatite deposits in the Kaustinen-Kokkola region (Syväjärvi, Rapasaari, Outovesi, Emmes and Läntinen). Figures differ between feasibility study updates and Sibanye-Stillwater's later reporting.
- **Mineral resources:** larger, on the order of 13-17 million tonnes at about 1% Li₂O, including measured, indicated and inferred categories.
- **Scale of operation:** the reserves are enough for about 12-15 years of production. The planned output is about 15,000 tonnes a year of battery-grade lithium hydroxide, enough for roughly 500,000 EVs.

Sibanye-Stillwater, which acquired Keliber in 2021, publishes updated figures in its annual Mineral Resources and Mineral Reserves report. Check the latest edition for current numbers.
B-keliber-reserve.web:
Keliber's ore reserve figure depends on the source and date. The most recent estimates I found are about 12.7 million tonnes.

- **Latest widely cited figure:** Open-pit and underground ore reserves of 12.7 million tonnes (0.92% lithium oxide) and mineral resources of 17 million tonnes (1.02% lithium oxide) support an estimated 16-year life of mine. That is from a March 2024 project update.
- **Sibanye-Stillwater's attributable figure:** The company's year-end 2022 technical report summary reports reserves based on its attributable interest of 84.96% in Keliber. This is why some of its numbers are lower. One interview cites mineral reserves of 8.2 million tonnes (grade 1.0%).
- **Finnish Minerals Group figure:** Its website lists 21.6 Mt of estimated proven and probable ore reserves. The page doesn't say what basis or date this uses, so I wouldn't compare it directly with the other figures.

Earlier estimates were smaller, as the deposits were still being drilled out:
- 7.46 Mt grading 1.04% lithium oxide, as of January 2019.
- A rise from 9.37 million tonnes to 12.3 Mt at an average grade of 0.94% lithium oxide. This was a later update.

Reserve figures vary with the reporting standard, the ownership share used and the update date. For the exact current number, check Sibanye-Stillwater's latest annual mineral resource and reserve statement.

ours.text:
Keliber's ore reserves, from Sibanye-Stillwater's S-K 1300 Technical Report Summary (effective 31 December 2024, issued April 2025), total about 13 Mt of ore:

| Category | Tonnage | Grade | Contained lithium (LCE) |

| Proven | 4.34 Mt | 1.09% Li2O | 117,000 t |

The total is my sum of the two categories, which the report does not state as a single figure. The reserves are stated on a 100% project basis. Sibanye-Stillwater's attributable interest is 79.82%, so its share would be about 79.82% of these figures. The reserve estimate was prepared by VBKOM (Pty) Ltd as Competent Person.

The report also contains mineral resources, but I did not pull those figures here, so I can't give resource totals.

B-dumont-econ.plain:
I can't give you reliable figures for this one. The most recent full feasibility study I know of is the 2019 update by Royal Nickel Corporation (now Karora Resources), which revised the 2013 study. I remember it showing a post-tax NPV (8% discount rate) of roughly US$1 billion and a post-tax IRR in the high teens. I'm not confident in those numbers, and they depend heavily on the nickel price and exchange rate assumptions.

The project has also changed hands since then. Waterton Global Resource Management now holds it through Dumont Nickel, and there may be newer technical work I'm not aware of.

For exact figures, check the NI 43-101 technical report on SEDAR+ for the project, or the Royal Nickel/Karora press release announcing the updated feasibility study. Any newer announcements from Dumont Nickel or Waterton would supersede those.
B-dumont-econ.web:
The most recent study I could find with published figures is the 2019 updated feasibility study. It gives a post-tax NPV (8% discount rate) of US$920 million and a post-tax IRR of 15.4%.

The study showed IRR improving from 15.2% to 15.4%, with a project NPV8% of $920 million. NPV and IRR were calculated from the assumed start of construction and based on 2019 H1 real costs. In Canadian dollars, the post-tax NPV8% was C$1,226 million, against C$1,330 million for the 2013 study. The full NI 43-101 technical report was filed in July 2019 after the May 30, 2019 announcement.

This study updated the 2013 feasibility study, which had a post-tax NPV8% of US$1,137 million and a post-tax IRR of 15.2%.

There is a newer study that I couldn't get figures for. Dumont Nickel LP's July 27, 2026 news release cites a "Dumont Nickel Feasibility Study, June 2026." That release said the company is targeting about 25,000 tonnes of nickel a year over an operating life of more than 45 years, with production starting in 2030. I couldn't find the NPV or IRR from that study in my search results. Check Dumont Nickel's website (dumontnickel.com), which has an economic summary, or its SEDAR+ filings for those numbers.

ours.text:
The most recent Dumont feasibility study in our data is the updated NI 43-101 Feasibility Study of 11 July 2019, prepared by RNC Minerals with Ausenco. It gives these post-tax results:

- **Post-tax NPV at an 8% discount rate:** US$920 million (C$1,226 million).
- **Post-tax IRR:** 15.4%.

**Study assumptions**
- The study assumed a long-term nickel price of US$7.75/lb.
- It describes a 30-year project life, with throughput of 52.5 ktpd initially, doubling from year 6.
- Peak funding was US$1,039 million (C$1,386 million).

**Caveats**
- The study is from 2019, so its price, capex and cost assumptions are old.
- I haven't checked whether a later update has been published, and none is in our data.

B-dumont-resource.plain:
I can't give you a figure I'm confident in. As I recall, the Dumont deposit (Launay and Trécesson townships, Abitibi, Quebec) has a measured and indicated resource of roughly 1.5-1.7 billion tonnes grading about 0.27% nickel. That is a very large, low-grade disseminated awaruite-type deposit. I believe the cut-off was in the 0.15-0.20% Ni range, but I'm not sure of the exact value.

The numbers changed between technical reports, including the Royal Nickel feasibility study and its later updates under Waterton/Magneto. The cut-off may also be stated differently, for example as a nickel-in-concentrate or Davis Tube-based figure. For an exact figure, check the most recent NI 43-101 technical report on SEDAR+. It will give the tonnage, grade, and cut-off by category.
B-dumont-resource.web:
Dumont's measured and indicated (M&I) resource is about 1.67 billion tonnes, reported at a cut-off grade of 0.15% nickel. This comes from the 2019 updated feasibility study (SRK, May 2019), which is the most recent full resource statement I found.

- **Tonnage and grade:** The measured resource is 372 million tonnes at 0.28% nickel, and the indicated resource is 1.29 billion tonnes at 0.26% nickel. Together that is 1,665,600 thousand tonnes, or about 1.67 Bt. The company's website now rounds this to 1.62 billion tonnes of measured and indicated mineral resources.
- **Contained metal:** The M&I category holds about 9.75 billion pounds of nickel. The 2019 release also lists about 394 million pounds of cobalt.
- **Cut-off:** The resource is reported at a cut-off grade of 0.15 percent nickel inside conceptual pit shells. The shells were optimized at a nickel price of US$7.50/lb and an average metallurgical recovery of 43%. Cobalt, palladium, platinum and magnetite are by-products, so they aren't counted in the cut-off calculation.
- **Overlap with reserves:** The M&I resources include the portion that was converted to mineral reserves. Reserves are a subset of the M&I figure and shouldn't be added to it.

ours.text:
The Dumont nickel deposit's **Measured** resource is **372.1 million tonnes at 0.28% Ni**, containing about **1,050 kt of nickel**. The cut-off grade is **0.15% Ni**.

The **Indicated** resource is 1,293.5 Mt at 0.26% Ni (3,380 kt Ni), at the same 0.15% Ni cut-off.

Both estimates are dated 30 May 2019, follow NI 43-101 (CIM 2014), and were prepared by SRK Consulting (Canada). The Measured and Indicated figures come from the report summarised in our library (document 380). The estimate is about seven years old, so check for any later update before relying on it.

B-vittangi-resource.plain:
I can't give you the Indicated and Inferred figures with confidence. As I recall, Talga's Vittangi graphite Mineral Resource (Nunasvaara and Jalkunen deposits, JORC 2012) totals roughly 30 to 35 million tonnes at about 24% graphitic carbon. That is on the order of 7 to 8 million tonnes of contained graphite, split between Indicated and Inferred. I don't remember the exact split, and I don't want to invent numbers.

The resource has been updated several times, and the Nunasvaara South Ore Reserve is reported separately from the Mineral Resource. The authoritative breakdown is in Talga's most recent ASX announcements, annual report Mineral Resource statement, or the Vittangi Graphite page on talgagroup.com.

If you can share the document or date you're working from, I can help interpret the figures.

| Category | Tonnage | Grade | Contained graphite |
|---|---|---|---|
| Indicated | 26,691,000 t (about 26.7 Mt) | 24.3% Cg | 6,482,000 t |
| Inferred | 8,329,000 t (about 8.3 Mt) | 22.1% Cg | 1,844,000 t |

These figures match the company's resource table, which lists the Indicated and Inferred totals by deposit. The resources are reported within preliminary pit shells and above a cut-off grade of 12.5% Cg.

Talga's wider Swedish graphite resources also include the Jalkunen and Raitajärvi deposits. Including those, the total is 70.8 Mt at 18.8% Cg, made up of 30.1 Mt Indicated and 40.7 Mt Inferred. The 35.0 Mt figure above covers only the Vittangi project.

I found no newer resource update in the search results. The company's July 2025 fact sheet still cites the 35 Mt at 23.8% Cg estimate.

Talga's Vittangi graphite Mineral Resource, as at 20 July 2023 (JORC 2012, estimated by SLR Consulting), is:

| Category | Tonnage | Graphite grade | Contained graphite |
|---|---|---|---|
| Indicated | 26.7 Mt | 24.3% Cg | 6.48 Mt |
| Inferred | 8.3 Mt | 22.1% Cg | 1.84 Mt |

B-amitsoq-resource.plain:
I can't give you exact, current figures with confidence.

**What I recall**
- GreenRoc Mining (AIM: GRL) reports a JORC (2012) Mineral Resource for Amitsoq, on Greenland's southern tip near Nanortalik.
- The resource is in the tens of millions of tonnes, with a high flake graphite grade of roughly mid-to-high teens percent total graphitic carbon (TGC). It is split between Indicated and Inferred categories.
- It underpins the company's pre-feasibility and later development studies, and GreenRoc has pursued the exploitation (mining) license and offtake and financing discussions.

**What I'm unsure about**
- I don't reliably remember the exact tonnage, grade, contained graphite, or classification split, so I won't quote numbers that might be wrong.
- I can't say whether there has been a more recent resource update or conversion to reserves, or how it compares with earlier estimates. My information may be out of date.

**Where to check**
- The GreenRoc website (investor and project pages) and its RNS announcements on the London Stock Exchange. Look for the "Mineral Resource Estimate" and "Competent Person's Report" releases.
- The most recent technical reports or studies (PFS or feasibility), which restate the resource and any Ore Reserve.
- The company's latest annual report or investor presentation, which usually has a summary table.

If you paste the figures or announcement text, I can help interpret them, for example by comparing resource versions or explaining Indicated versus Inferred.
B-amitsoq-resource.web:
**Current JORC resource:** Amitsoq has a combined Measured, Indicated and Inferred JORC resource of 23.05 million tonnes at an average grade of 20.41% graphite. That equates to about 4.71 Mt of contained graphite.

**Has it been updated recently?** No. The 23.05 Mt figure is still the official number, and an update is pending.
- The global JORC-compliant estimate was announced on 23 January 2023. Before that, the resource was smaller. A 2022 announcement cited a combined Indicated and Inferred resource of 8.28 Mt at 19.75% graphite.
- GreenRoc announced on 27 October 2026 that it had completed Phase III drilling. Eight holes were drilled, and all three drilling platforms showed significant intersections of graphite ore.
- That drilling was meant in part to increase the confidence level of the coming revised Resource Estimate. The company has therefore flagged a revised estimate but hasn't yet published one, as far as these results show.
- Earlier results showed that Phase III drilling extended the lower graphite layer 100 to 150 meters north of the earlier resource drilling area.
- The company has said it has gathered enough data for a Pre-Feasibility Study planned for Q1 2027.

Check GreenRoc's RNS announcements for the revised estimate, since it could come out soon.

ours.text:
**Current JORC resource (January 2023 estimate):** 23.05 million tonnes at 20.41% graphitic carbon, containing 4.71 Mt of graphite. The split by confidence:

| Category | Tonnes (Mt) | Graphitic carbon | Contained graphite (Mt) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Measured | 1.26 | 22.05% | 0.28 |
| Indicated | 6.12 | 21.04% | 1.29 |
| Inferred | 15.67 | 20.04% | 3.14 |
| **Total** | **23.05** | **20.41%** | **4.71** |

It is reported under JORC 2012 with a zero cut-off grade. The competent person is Dr John Arthur. The estimate covers the Amitsoq Island deposit.

**Has it been updated?** Not yet. The 2023 figure is the most recent one, and it is still the figure GreenRoc cites. It replaced the maiden estimate of March 2022 (8.28 Mt at 19.75%, 1.63 Mt graphite), which is now superseded.

The company's 27 October 2026 update (GreenRoc Strategic Materials Plc, formerly GreenRoc Mining) says the 2023 estimate is still the global JORC figure. It completed Phase III drilling, with eight holes drilled out of ten planned, and says the drilling was meant to support a revised resource estimate. The main aim was to convert the roughly 2.1 Mt of Inferred material in the 2023 preliminary economic assessment into higher-confidence categories. No revised estimate has been announced. The company plans a pre-feasibility study starting in Q1 2027.

The company's own announcements are the source for the 2023 figures and the 2026 status. Our database holds the 2023 rows, and I did not find a newer estimate in the ingested documents.
